name: desire for order
quote: A place for everything, everything in its place.
description: Wanting things match a particular ideal or at least be withing a particular range of expectations.

variations.name: desire for social order
variations.description: Wanting people to behave as expected.

variations.name: desire for pure body
variations.description: A desire to align with the ideal that your body is a temple: eating well, exercising, sleeping well, etc.

variations.name: desire for pure social reputation
variations.description: A desire to bolter and protect an aspect of an identity as a way to ensure social status.
examples: Doing things to be seen as brave.
Striving for perfect competence in a field.

variations.name: desire for pure existential reputation
variations.description: A desire for a spotless reputation. While you can hide thoughts from people, your existential self knows it can't hide them from God, karma, or the Universe.
examples: Modern religious people may strive for goodness, faith, and charity.
Ancient religions may have encouraged aggression and bravery without hesitation.

variations.name: desire for pure perception
variations.description: A desire to perceive key parts of the world clearly to improve the chance of choosing the correct actions.

variations.name: desire for pure environment
variations.description: Wanting to live in an environment that supports key purities
examples: Wanting to stay away from liars who pollute your ability to perceive clearly.
Wanting to live in a clean place with safe water.

commentaries.quote: Many of us have ideals that we work very hard to live up to. Sometimes we can become obsessive about aligning with an ideal as a way of hoping to control negative things in our lives.

There's a lot of overlap underlying our desires for social status, purity, safety, and comfort. It may be worth considering whether the strength of these desires is helping you or causing unnecessary stress.

conditions: You have a strong desire to live up a particular ideal.
